description: My name is Troy Boussarath. This is my first Hackathon. I’m good at developing full-stack. I’ve developed a website from scratch called TannerPlayz.com. I know how to use CloudFlare to create a domain, AWS and Ubuntu to run servers, and how to create an automated system through GitHub that pushes all of  the changes.
summary: Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer is a browser game where 3 kids train for a lunar south pole mission like a D&D campaign. An AI Dungeon Master, Magic the Tanner 🎩, narrates whatever the players try, reads their d20 rolls, and reacts to their ideas. The crew explores 5 real south pole locations, including Artemis III candidate regions, a permanently shadowed crater and the site of NASA's LCROSS impact. They fight moon bugs, search for gear, talk to NPC astronauts at moon bases, and defeat a Giant Moon Worm. Every cleared location unlocks a real NASA fact with its source. I time-boxed the build to about 2 hours to show how much one person can ship quickly with clear priorities and AI as a tool.
details:
How it works

- Frontend: plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript with a minimalist look; sound effects are synthesized in the browser with the Web Audio API.

- Backend: Node.js + Express. The browser never talks to the AI directly: it sends the game state to my own /api/dm endpoint, and the server calls Google Gemini with the DM's rules.

- The server enforces the rules, not the AI: damage comes from the dice, the AI can't conjure items, searching requires standing next to the spot, enemies only react when targeted, and the boss needs at least 4 hits.

- Safety: the endpoint is rate limited (per player plus a daily cap), the API key stays only on the server, and a backup DM keeps the game playable if the AI is down. Kid-friendly content rules are built into the DM.

- Tested with 18 automated Node tests and full headless-browser playthroughs. Hosted on AWS EC2 with Nginx, PM2 and Cloudflare.

- Code: https://github.com/Troyota2/spaceapps-tannerplayz

Why it matters

Kids learn by playing. Every location teaches a real fact from NASA's lunar south pole research: where Artemis III might land, why some craters never see sunlight, and how LCROSS proved there is water ice on the Moon. The humor and "you can't really lose" design make it safe for young players to experiment.

Time limit

I signed up and only remembered the night before, so I gave myself a strict build window of about 2 hours (3:27 to 5:45 PM, logged in the README). To stay in scope I cut online 3-device multiplayer, custom art (emoji are used as sprites) and save/load.

Credits

DM style inspired by Magic the Noah's D&D videos (inspiration only; no names, voices, catchphrases or content are used). No NASA logos, insignia or mission patches are used.
